title: Removals That Balance Even and Odd Slots
statement:
You get an integer array nums. You will delete exactly one element; everything after it moves one place to the left.

The result is balanced when the sum of the values at even indexes (0, 2, 4, …) equals the sum of the values at odd indexes (1, 3, 5, …). An empty array is balanced: both sums are 0.

Return how many indexes you could delete to get a balanced array.

examples.why: Only deleting the last element works: [2, 5, 3] has 2 + 3 = 5 on even slots and 5 on odd slots.
Any deletion leaves [4, 4], which is balanced.
Delete index 0: [2, 3, 1] gives 2 + 1 = 3 against 3. Delete index 2: [1, 2, 1] gives 2 against 2. The elements after the deleted one switch parity, so you cannot just subtract from the original sums.

hints: When you delete index i, what happens to the elements before i? And to the ones after it?
Elements before i keep their parity. Elements after i swap: what was on an even slot is now on an odd slot, and the other way round.
With prefix sums of even-slot and odd-slot values, the new even sum is evenBefore(i) + oddAfter(i) and the new odd sum is oddBefore(i) + evenAfter(i). Each check is O(1).

explain.intuition:
Deleting index i leaves the prefix before it untouched and shifts the suffix after it by one place, which flips the parity of every suffix element. So the new even sum is the even-slot part of the prefix plus the odd-slot part of the suffix, and the new odd sum is the other two parts.

Keep running totals of even and odd values seen so far, and the totals still ahead. Walking left to right, each index moves from "ahead" to "before" and can be checked in constant time, like keeping a running counter instead of recounting a list on every render.
steps: Compute evenAhead and oddAhead: the sums over all even and odd indexes.
Set evenBefore = oddBefore = 0. For each index i, first remove nums[i] from the ahead total of its parity.
Add nums[i] to the before total of its parity and move on.
pitfalls: Forgetting the parity flip and comparing totalEven − x with totalOdd. It happens to work for the last index only.
Leaving nums[i] in the ahead sums when checking index i. The deleted value belongs to neither side.
Rebuilding the array for every deletion, which is O(n²) on 100 000 elements.

solutions.title: Delete and recount
solutions.idea: For each index, build the array without it and sum the even and odd slots.

solutions.title: Running sums before and ahead
solutions.idea: Before the deleted index parities stay; after it they swap. Track both parities on both sides and compare in O(1).

followups: Delete exactly two elements instead. How many pairs balance the array, and can you do better than O(n²)?
Values can change between queries. Which data structure keeps the prefix sums fresh?
